notice: This file maps canonical laboratories to the engineering domains and operating modes they require. It is a coverage plan. It is not evidence that any model, engine, or laboratory is operational, and it never grants assessment eligibility or publication approval. Laboratory identity and lifecycle remain owned by data/lmf/lab-registry.json.

labs.notes: Charging-system and general circuit relationships. Regulated charging behaviour and source/load conditions are not yet modelled numerically.
First pilot. Electrical nodal analysis is the first engine. Starter-motor mechanical behaviour is explicitly out of scope and disclosed as a simplification.
Relay coil and contact behaviour with switched loads. Reuses the electrical engine and the relay coupling contract.
Sensor supply, ground, reference voltage and analog or frequency signals. Signal connections are excluded from the DC solve and routed to a signal-aware adapter.
PWM actuator operation, duty cycle and driver control. PWM requires a declared pwmModel before entering the DC solve.
Requires a dedicated network domain engine. Protocol simulation must remain explicitly distinct from physical-layer electrical simulation; the electrical solver must never answer a bus question.
Distinct voltage domains with isolation boundaries. Cross-domain paths without a modelled converter must fail closed. Training-only safety notices required for traction domains.
Compression, cylinder leakage, valve timing and mechanical efficiency. Requires a mechanical engine and a separate validation method.
Hydraulic pressure and force transmission. ABS interactions require a separately validated model before inclusion.
Steering geometry, wheel alignment and suspension behaviour. Geometry units and sign conventions must be declared before implementation.
Torque transfer, gear ratios, clutch behaviour and differential operation.
Hydraulic, mechanical, electronic-control and thermal relationships. Simplified models must be explicitly distinguished from manufacturer-specific behaviour.
Multi-domain laboratory requiring thermal, electrical and fluid models together. Refrigerant-model assumptions must be stated explicitly. First integrated pilot target is the cooling-fan scenario.
Combustion fundamentals, fuel and ignition behaviour, and OBD-II data interpretation.
Emission-control fundamentals, catalyst concepts, EVAP diagnostics and monitor readiness.
Sensor and vehicle-motion concepts, calibration principles and system limitations. A virtual calibration must never be presented as equivalent to a manufacturer-approved physical calibration.
Integrated problems requiring primary fault, secondary effect and misleading symptom discrimination. Requires multi-domain composition governance before implementation.
